resources.string: Lets Notification Sync tell you when something goes wrong, and lets you send test notifications from Tools.

Notification Sync mirrors your phone\'s notifications on your Pebble. It works in the background, so it asks for everything it needs now. Each step is optional, but notifications only reach the watch once Notification Access and Pebble App Access are on.

Notification Sync reads the notifications on this phone, including the app, sender, message text and attached pictures, so it can show them on your Pebble and let you act on them from the watch.
They are only sent to your watch over Bluetooth. Nothing is uploaded, shared or stored anywhere else, and the app has no internet access.

Notification Sync will read the notifications on this phone (app, sender, text and pictures) and send them only to your Pebble, over Bluetooth.

Android will ask you to pick a nearby device. Pick anything in the list; it does not need to be a Pebble. This is only how Android lets companion apps read notifications reliably.

Right after that, Android opens the Notification Access screen. Turn Notification Sync on there.

Android blocks this for apps installed from a file. To allow it:

1. Tap Open App Info below.
2. Tap the ⋮ menu in the top right corner.
3. Tap Allow restricted settings and confirm.
4. Come back here and tap Open Notification Access.
